title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Call Centre Agent
description:
EE Merthyr Tydfil Contact Centre - Full-time role - 37.5 Hours per week

If you're outgoing, full of energy and love talking to people, you'd be better off in sales with EE.

Maybe you've worked in retail, or hospitality before. You know how to deal with customers but you're looking for something more exciting - a job that's going to challenge you. And, of course, you want to earn a bit more cash.

Our team in Merthyr is full of people like you - so you'll be in great company here.

What does being a sales advisor involve?

You'll join a lively sales team in our Merthyr contact centre. We'll train you to take incoming calls from existing EE customers and help them find the best deals on their phones and broadband. You'll also help them to navigate the different tech products we sell.

You need to be a great listener as well as a fluent talker. A lot of the time, you'll pick up on something that someone has said, then use that to match them with the perfect product.

Forget what you've heard about sales

Don't let what you've heard about sales put you off. Let's smash a few myths
- Yes, there are targets to hit. But the kind of people who like sales, love that. You're probably naturally competitive. You get a buzz out of beating the person next to you. You hate being bored at work.
- It's not "cold calling". The calls come in to you and you decide how best you can help the customer. That's why we value resourceful people who like fixing problems.
- People say it's "hard selling". It's really not! You're basically talking to people about fun tech stuff that they already want. Who doesn't love a better phone, faster broadband or a new console?

Why you'll be better off at EE

GREAT MONEY - you start on £26,116 which goes up to £26,738 after 8 months.

UNCAPPED COMMISSION - the more you sell, the more you can earn.

BRILLIANT BENEFITS - including 24/7 GP appointments for you and your family, free parking and discounts on EE products like phones and broadband that could save you £100s every year.

GROWTH - we're passionate about developing our people. There are plenty of career paths across EE and BT.

FLEXIBILITY - you can bank hours then take time off when you need. Plus, generous leave for carers and anyone starting a family.

GREAT PEOPLE - you're working with people like you. It's a sociable, supportive environment.

title: Family Paralegal
description:
Family Paralegal

Cardiff or Swansea

Permanent

Monday to Friday

Salary - DOE

Introduction

Acorn by Synergie is recruiting a Family Paralegal on behalf of our client to join their busy Family Law team. This is an excellent opportunity for a proactive and ambitious individual to gain wide-ranging experience across family law, including divorce, financial matters, child arrangements, and cases involving domestic abuse. The role also provides a strong platform for those aiming to secure a Training Contract and qualify as a solicitor.

Key Duties
- Support solicitors in managing a caseload of family law matters.
- Prepare and draft legal documents, including correspondence, applications, and witness statements.
- Carry out legal research and stay updated on family law developments.
- Liaise with clients, counsel, and other stakeholders under supervision.
- Maintain accurate and well-organised client files and records.
- Assist with the assembly of court documents and attend court when required.
- Contribute to negotiations and mediation processes.
- Support day-to-day administration, including managing documentation, calendars, and billing.

Requirements
- Law degree (LLB or equivalent) and completion of LPC (or equivalent route).
- Interest in family law; previous paralegal or legal assistant experience preferred.
- Strong legal research skills and ability to present information clearly.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with sensitivity in dealing with vulnerable clients.
- Exceptional organisational skills with the ability to manage competing deadlines.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Resilience and ability to work effectively in a busy environment.
- Clear ambition to secure a Training Contract and qualify as a solicitor.

Attitudes & Behaviours
- Client-Focused: Dedicated to delivering high-quality service and client care.
- Professional Integrity: Respecting confidentiality and ethical standards.
- Initiative: Proactive in supporting the team and taking responsibility.
- Teamwork: Positive and collaborative approach to colleagues.
- Ambition: Motivated to develop professionally and progress within the firm.

Interested?

Apply now to join a leading Family Law team in Cardiff and develop your career as a Family Paralegal.

Acorn by Synergie acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment.

title: Planner and Scheduler - Taffs Well
description:
About The Role
Planner & Scheduler
Location: Taffs Well
Salary: Competitive

The Role

We are looking for a highly organised, analytical, and proactive Planner & Scheduler to join our PHS Hygiene team.

In this role, you will play a key part in ensuring our Service Drivers operate on optimised routes, our customers receive outstanding service, and our operational performance consistently meets the highest standards.

Working closely with the Lead Scheduler and Operations Management teams, you will help drive continuous improvement, efficiency, and excellent customer outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

As a Planner & Scheduler, you will:
- Create and maintain optimal schedules for Service Drivers to maximise productivity and resource utilisation.
- Analyse routes and driver feedback to continuously improve efficiency.
- Monitor unplanned work and KPI trends to ensure resources are used effectively.
- Maintain backlogs at appropriate levels to support operational performance.
- Work collaboratively with operational teams to ensure service delivery targets are achieved.
- Identify opportunities for continuous improvement and implement effective scheduling solutions.
- Support operational planning activities to ensure excellent customer service.

About You

The ideal candidate will have:
- Advanced knowledge of scheduling systems and scheduling best practices.
- Strong IT skills and a passion for technology.
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.
- A customer-focused approach, taking ownership of scheduling delivery for assigned Operations Centres.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills with a collaborative working style.
- The ability to prioritise workloads and perform effectively under pressure.
- A resilient and proactive attitude with a positive, can-do approach.
- A valid UK driving licence (essential).

What We Offer

In return for your commitment and expertise, you will receive:
- Competitive salary
- Virtual GP service for you and your household
- Buy and sell holiday scheme
- Access to PHS Perks, offering discounts with major supermarkets and retailers
- Ongoing training and development opportunities
- Accredited ILM qualifications through both external and in-house training
- Apprenticeship opportunities
- 23 days annual leave plus bank holidays (31 days in total)
- Free on-site parking
- Enhanced parental and paternity leave
- 24-hour wellbeing helpline
- Cycle to Work scheme
- Pension scheme
- Life assurance
- Additional employee benefits

About PHS Group

Founded in 1963, PHS Group is the leading provider of hygiene services across the UK, Ireland, and Spain. We support more than 90,000 customers across 300,000 locations and have built a reputation for delivering essential workplace services over more than six decades.

At PHS, we are proud of our diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued, respected, and able to bring their authentic selves to work without fear of discrimination.

PHS is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all backgrounds and communities.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
The Accounts Assistant role in Cardiff is all about keeping things running smoothly in the accounting and finance department of a business services organisation. You'll handle day-to-day financial tasks, helping to ensure everything balances and operates efficiently.

Client Details

As a business services organisation based in Cardiff.Our client is a well-established international organisation that delivers specialist services to governments, public sector bodies, and global businesses across Europe. With a collaborative and supportive culture, they combine the stability of an established business with the opportunity to gain exposure to international operations, making it an excellent environment for career development and long-term growth.

Description
- Process invoices and payments accurately and on time.
- Reconcile bank statements and monitor accounts for discrepancies.
- Assist with preparing financial reports and management accounts.
- Maintain and update financial records in line with company policies.
- Support the month-end and year-end closing processes.
- Respond to internal and external financial queries promptly and professionally.
- Collaborate with colleagues to ensure compliance with accounting regulations.
- Provide general administrative support to the accounting and finance team.

Profile

A successful Accounts Assistant should have:
- A good understanding of basic accounting principles.
- Experience using accounting software and financial systems.
- Strong numerical skills and attention to detail.
- The ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Good organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and a willingness to learn.

Job Offer
- Salary of £30,000
- Yearly bonus.
- Cycle to work scheme.
- Private health care.
- Potential study support.

title: HR Coordinator
description:
Are you an organised HR professional who enjoys supporting colleagues, advising managers and keeping People processes running smoothly?

We're recruiting a People Co-ordinator on behalf of a confidential client. This varied role offers the opportunity to support the full employee lifecycle, provide first-line HR guidance and help improve the way People services are delivered.

Reporting to the Head of People Services, you'll be a key point of contact for managers and colleagues, combining day-to-day HR administration with support for employee relations, payroll and compliance.

What you'll be doing
- Coordinating onboarding, contracts, employee changes, probation and leaver processes.
- Responding to People queries and providing guidance on policies and procedures.
- Supporting managers with absence, informal performance concerns and minor conduct matters, escalating complex cases appropriately.
- Coordinating meetings, taking notes and preparing documentation for formal HR processes.
- Supporting payroll administration and maintaining accurate, confidential employee records.
- Coordinating right to work checks, visa documentation and compliance monitoring.
- Helping review and update People policies, procedures and guidance.
- Contributing to HR systems improvements, automation, reporting and wider People projects.

What you'll bring
- Experience in an HR or People role, such as HR Co-ordinator, HR Officer or People Advisor.
- A strong understanding of employee lifecycle administration and HR processes.
- Experience supporting low-level employee relations matters.
- Experience coordinating right to work and visa compliance processes, alongside payroll administration.
- Confidence using HR systems and maintaining accurate employee data.
- Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Clear communication, sound judgement and a helpful, service-focused approach.
- An understanding of employment legislation and HR best practice.
- An interest in improving systems, processes and the colleague experience.

CIPD Level 5, or working towards it, and a relevant HR or administration qualification would be desirable.

The role is based in Cardiff with hybrid working, with travel to operational sites where required.

Interested? Apply with your CV to be considered for this People Co-ordinator opportunity. The client's identity will be shared at the appropriate stage of the recruitment process.
